title: Лёва в роли Шефа  (Lyova Playing the Role of the Chef)

segments.t: While Sasha tells Max that she could not stay with her aunt, the VIP guest's assistant slips past the dining room and heads straight into the kitchen demanding to see the chef. Thinking fast, the crew shoves Lyova into the office so he can pretend to be Viktor Petrovich.
Там какая-то девушка сюда идет, хочет видеть шефа.
Где я могу найти вашего шеф-повара?
Я же просил меня не беспокоить.
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
'Did it not work out staying at your aunt's place?' Barinov presses sharply if there is more going on behind the scenes.
'Yes, her father-in-law is coming to visit her.' Addressing the mother law in front of Barinov, Kostya leans on "priyezzhayet" ("is arriving", a form of "priyezzhat") to give the remark its edge.
'So it did not work out.' Leaning in warmly in the exchange, the "-sya" ending on "poluchilos" ("worked out") marks an action that unfolds mutually or turns back on the speaker.
'All right then.' Kostya directly shares this word of agreement toward Barinov using "ladno" ("alright") — built from the old Russian root for harmony and order, used every day for "okay, fine".
'Well, it is no big deal.' Describing how terrible things are in the exchange, Barinov leans on "strashnogo" ("terrible, serious", a form of "strashnyy") to give the remark its edge.
'Maybe.' Reacting frankly to Barinov, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
Там какая-то девушка сюда идет, хочет видеть шефа.
'Some woman is walking this way, she wants to see the Chef.' Barinov answers earnestly with a shrug, bringing things back to earth after the buildup.
'We stick to the plan.' Bringing up the plan with Barinov, Kostya reaches for the Russian word "rabotayem" ("we work, let's work", built from "rabotat") right at the center of the line.
Где я могу найти вашего шеф-повара?
'Where can I find your head chef?' Touching on the head right here, Barinov puts the question word "gde" right at the start so Kostya hears the focus immediately.

'In his office, of course.' Kostya plainly delivers this confirmation as they meet using "konechno" ("of course") — spoken with a soft "shn" sound in everyday Moscow Russian to mean "of course, certainly".
Я же просил меня не беспокоить.
'I specifically asked not to be disturbed.' Barinov continues vividly in the exchange and puts the emphasis on "bespokoit" ("to bother") in the middle of the talk.
'I am preparing the new menu.' Pointing to the new menu with Barinov, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 4 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Close that damn door!' Barinov steps in frankly across the room, letting the remark speak for itself.
Там какая-то девушка сюда идет, хочет видеть шефа.
Где я могу найти вашего шеф-повара?
Я же просил меня не беспокоить.

That wraps up this scene as when the VIP's assistant sneaks into the kitchen looking for the head chef, Vika and the cooks push Lyova into Barinov's office to impersonate Viktor Petrovich. See you next time!
